QuestionStmt.S: In a triangle ABC with usual notations, if a, b, c are in arithmetic progression, then $\tan \frac{A}{2} \cdot \tan \frac{C}{2} =$

Solution.S:
Given $a, b, c$ are in AP, so $a + c = 2b$.

Semi-perimeter $s = \frac{a + b + c}{2} = \frac{3b}{2}$.

Half-angle formula: $\tan \frac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}$, $\tan \frac{C}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{(s-a)(s-b)}{s(s-c)}}$.

Thus:

$$\tan \frac{A}{2} \cdot \tan \frac{C}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)} \cdot \frac{(s-a)(s-b)}{s(s-c)}} = \frac{s-b}{s}$$

$$= \frac{\frac{3b}{2} - b}{\frac{3b}{2}} = \frac{\frac{b}{2}}{\frac{3b}{2}} = \frac{1}{3}$$

Hence the correct option is D: $\frac{1}{3}$.
